source.accroche: Longevity Tierlist For Optimal Health (Science based)

notes: Full test du 24/11 : « Longevity Tierlist For Optimal Health (Science based) », sa famille à 98 k (28/10) ; éléments à nous. Croquis de couverture neuf (longevite.jpg, Seedream). Slide Atala (11) : le second A tier « Running A Few Times A Week », deux coureuses de la banque et le logo d'Atala. Texte selon placement_atala : voix TU ; un seul argument : la semaine complète, avec le renforcement prévu dedans ; version « cta G' ». Faits : sédentarité prolongée et mortalité (Ekelund et al., Lancet 2016) ; sommeil court et risque cardiovasculaire et mortalité (Cappuccio et al., Sleep 2010) ; solitude et mortalité, effet comparable à des facteurs de risque majeurs (Holt-Lunstad et al., PLoS Med 2010) ; bénéfice des pas qui plafonne vers 6 000 à 10 000 selon l'âge (Paluch et al., Lancet Public Health 2022) ; marche après repas et glycémie (Buffey et al., Sports Med 2022) ; 120 min par semaine dans la nature (White et al., Sci Rep 2019) ; perte de masse musculaire avec l'âge et renforcement associé à une mortalité plus basse (Momma et al., Br J Sports Med 2022) ; coureurs : environ 3 ans d'espérance de vie en plus, même à faible volume (Lee et al., Prog Cardiovasc Dis 2017) ; Harvard Study of Adult Development (Waldinger). Rien de médical.

paragraphes: Long hours without moving slow down your metabolism and weaken the muscles that keep you independent later in life.
It's one of the habits most linked to a shorter life. Breaking it up is the first win.
Short sleep, night after night, is linked to a higher risk of heart problems and a shorter life.
No other habit on this list can make up for it.
Constant stress keeps your body on high alert. Over years, that wears down your heart, your sleep and your mood.
Stress itself isn't the problem. Never letting it out is.
Loneliness is linked to a shorter life about as strongly as some of the worst habits we know.
It's in D, not F, because it's the easiest to fix today.
Walking more is linked to living longer, but the benefit levels off well before the famous number.
Great habit. The exact number matters less than you'd think.
A few calm minutes a day can lower stress and help you sleep, which both matter for a long life.
Helpful, but the direct proof for a longer life is thin.
A short walk after eating helps your body handle the sugar from your meal, with almost no effort.
Small, easy, and it adds up over thousands of meals.
People who spend about two hours a week in nature report better health and wellbeing.
It misses A tier because it works best with real movement on top.
After 30, you slowly lose muscle every decade. Strength training slows that down, and stronger people tend to live longer.
Two sessions a week is enough to keep the muscle you'll need at 80.

en.nom: Running A Few Times A Week
paragraphes: Runners tend to live several years longer than non-runners, even at slow paces and low mileage.
The trick is the strength work too. A running coach app like Atala puts it into your week.
The longest study on adult life found that good relationships predict a long, healthy life best.
Nothing else on this list matters as much as that.
